title: 韦讽录事宅观曹将军画马图
title_en: Viewing General Cao's Painting of Horses at the Home of Recorder Wei Feng
author: 杜甫

text_note.zh: 这里用通行本（《唐诗三百首》常见的文本）。古籍文本第七、九句作“马脑盌”“盌赐”，是玛瑙碗；通行本作“玛瑙盘”“盘赐”，是玛瑙盘子。“婕妤”古籍写作“倢伃”，“狮子花”写作“师子花”，只是写法不同，意思一样。
text_note.en: This follows the commonly taught text, as found in the usual editions of Three Hundred Tang Poems. In lines seven and nine, the old corpus has an agate bowl; the taught text has an agate plate. The corpus also writes the palace lady's title jié yú and the horse's name "Lion Flower" with older forms of the characters, with the same meaning.

readings.zh: 读 shǔ，数一数、算得上的意思。“独数”就是只能算他。
readings.en: Read shǔ, to count. Dú shǔ means only he counts as the best.

readings.zh: 读 chéng。“乘黄”是传说中的神马。
readings.en: Read chéng. Chéng huáng is a magic horse of legend.

readings.zh: 读 mào。这里是动词，画像的意思。
readings.en: Read mào. Here it is a verb: to paint a likeness.

readings.zh: 读 yān，深红色。不读 yīn。
readings.en: Read yān, meaning deep red, not yīn.

readings.zh: 按现在的读法读 qí。古代“骑兵、骑战”的骑作名词时读 jì。
readings.en: Read qí as taught today. In old times, as a noun meaning cavalry, it was read jì.

readings.zh: 读 cháo，朝见、拜见的意思。
readings.en: Read cháo, meaning to go and pay respects.

glosses.zh: 国初：唐朝开国的时候。
glosses.en: guó chū: the start of the Tang dynasty.

glosses.zh: 已来：以来。
glosses.en: yǐ lái: since then.

glosses.zh: 鞍马：备着马鞍的马，这里指画马。
glosses.en: ān mǎ: saddled horses; here, paintings of horses.

glosses.zh: 神妙：画得神奇精妙。
glosses.en: shén miào: wonderfully skillful.

glosses.zh: 江都王：唐太宗的侄子李绪，被封为江都王，擅长画马。
glosses.en: jiāng dū wáng: the Prince of Jiangdu, Li Xu, a nephew of Emperor Taizong, who was good at painting horses.

glosses.zh: 将军：指曹霸。他做过左武卫将军，是唐玄宗时画马最有名的画家。
glosses.en: jiāng jūn: General Cao Ba, the most famous horse painter in the time of Emperor Xuanzong.

glosses.zh: 人间：人世间。
glosses.en: rén jiān: the human world.

glosses.zh: 乘黄：传说中的神马。这里说曹霸画的马就像真的神马。
glosses.en: chéng huáng: a magic horse of legend. Cao Ba's horses looked like real magic horses.

glosses.zh: 先帝：去世的皇帝，指唐玄宗。
glosses.en: xiān dì: the late emperor, Xuanzong.

glosses.zh: 照夜白：唐玄宗的一匹名马，白色。
glosses.en: zhào yè bái: Night-Shining White, a famous white horse of Emperor Xuanzong.

glosses.zh: 龙池：唐朝兴庆宫里的一个水池，传说有龙。
glosses.en: lóng chí: Dragon Pond, a pool in the Xingqing Palace, said to hold a dragon.

glosses.zh: 十日飞霹雳：一连十天打雷。夸张地说画上的马像真的一样，好像要变成龙飞走。
glosses.en: shí rì fēi pī lì: thunder for ten days, a playful way of saying the painted horse was so real it seemed about to turn into a dragon.

glosses.zh: 内府：皇宫的仓库。
glosses.en: nèi fǔ: the palace storehouse.

glosses.zh: 殷红：深红色。
glosses.en: yān hóng: deep red.

glosses.zh: 玛瑙盘：用玛瑙做的盘子。玛瑙是一种漂亮的宝石。
glosses.en: mǎ nǎo pán: a plate made of agate, a beautiful stone.

glosses.zh: 婕妤：宫中女官的一种名称。
glosses.en: jié yú: a rank of palace lady.

glosses.zh: 传诏：传达皇帝的命令。
glosses.en: chuán zhào: to pass on the emperor's order.

glosses.zh: 才人：宫中女官的一种名称。
glosses.en: cái rén: another rank of palace lady.

glosses.zh: 索：取来。
glosses.en: suǒ: to fetch.

glosses.zh: 拜舞：古代臣子感谢皇帝时的一种礼节，又拜又舞。
glosses.en: bài wǔ: a court ritual of bowing and dancing to thank the emperor.

glosses.zh: 轻纨细绮：轻薄精细的丝绸。古人请人作画，常常送上丝绸。
glosses.en: qīng wán xì qǐ: fine light silks. People sent silk when they wanted a painting.

glosses.zh: 相追飞：一个接一个地送来，像追着飞来一样。
glosses.en: xiāng zhuī fēi: coming one after another, as if flying after him.

glosses.zh: 贵戚权门：皇亲国戚和有权势的人家。
glosses.en: guì qī quán mén: royal relatives and powerful families.

glosses.zh: 笔迹：这里指曹霸的画。
glosses.en: bǐ jì: here, Cao Ba's paintings.

glosses.zh: 屏障：屏风。
glosses.en: píng zhàng: folding screens.

glosses.zh: 太宗：唐太宗李世民。
glosses.en: tài zōng: Emperor Taizong of Tang, Li Shimin.

glosses.zh: 拳毛䯄：唐太宗的一匹战马，毛是卷的。䯄是黄毛黑嘴的马。
glosses.en: quán máo guā: Curly-Haired Gua, a war horse of Emperor Taizong, with curly hair, yellow with a black mouth.

glosses.zh: 郭家：指名将郭子仪家。
glosses.en: guō jiā: the family of the great general Guo Ziyi.

glosses.zh: 狮子花：郭子仪得到的一匹名马。一说是唐代宗赐给他的。
glosses.en: shī zi huā: Lion Flower, a famous horse owned by Guo Ziyi, said to have been given to him by Emperor Daizong.

glosses.zh: 识者：懂马、懂画的人。
glosses.en: shí zhě: people who know horses and paintings.

glosses.zh: 叹嗟：感叹、赞叹。
glosses.en: tàn jiē: to sigh with admiration.

glosses.zh: 骑战：骑着马打仗。
glosses.en: qí zhàn: fighting on horseback.

glosses.zh: 一敌万：一匹马能抵得上一万匹。
glosses.en: yī dí wàn: one horse worth ten thousand.

glosses.zh: 缟素：白色的丝绢，画就画在上面。
glosses.en: gǎo sù: white silk, which the painting is on.

glosses.zh: 漠漠：广阔无边的样子。
glosses.en: mò mò: wide and endless.

glosses.zh: 开风沙：画面上好像展开了一片风沙。
glosses.en: kāi fēng shā: a scene of wind and sand seems to open up.

glosses.zh: 殊绝：特别出众，极好。
glosses.en: shū jué: outstanding, superb.

glosses.zh: 迥若：远远看去好像。
glosses.en: jiǒng ruò: from afar they look like.

glosses.zh: 寒空动烟雪：寒冷的天空里烟雾和雪花在飘动，形容马的毛色和奔跑的样子。
glosses.en: hán kōng dòng yān xuě: mist and snow moving in a cold sky, describing the horses' coats and motion.

glosses.zh: 霜蹄：马蹄。古书说马蹄能踏霜雪。
glosses.en: shuāng tí: horses' hooves. An old book says hooves can tread frost and snow.

glosses.zh: 蹴踏：踢踏、奔跑。
glosses.en: cù tà: to stamp and run.

glosses.zh: 长楸：道路两旁长长的楸树。楸树是一种高大的树。
glosses.en: cháng qiū: long rows of catalpa trees along a road.

glosses.zh: 马官：管马的官。
glosses.en: mǎ guān: officials who look after horses.

glosses.zh: 厮养：养马、喂马的仆人。
glosses.en: sī yǎng: grooms and stable hands.

glosses.zh: 森成列：整整齐齐地站成一排排。
glosses.en: sēn chéng liè: standing in neat rows.

glosses.zh: 可怜：可爱。古诗里常是这个意思。
glosses.en: kě lián: lovely. In old poems kě lián often means this.

glosses.zh: 神骏：神气、雄健。
glosses.en: shén jùn: spirited and strong.

glosses.zh: 顾视：回头看、左右看。
glosses.en: gù shì: looking around.

glosses.zh: 气深稳：气度沉着稳重。
glosses.en: qì shēn wěn: calm and steady in bearing.

glosses.zh: 借问：请问。
glosses.en: jiè wèn: may I ask.

glosses.zh: 苦心爱者：真心喜爱这幅画的人。
glosses.en: kǔ xīn ài zhě: the one who loves this painting with all his heart.

glosses.zh: 韦讽：这幅画的主人，杜甫的朋友。录事是他的官职。
glosses.en: wéi fěng: the owner of the painting, a friend of Du Fu. Recorder was his post.

glosses.zh: 支遁：东晋时的高僧，特别爱马，说自己看重的是马的神采。
glosses.en: zhī dùn: Zhi Dun, a famous monk of the Eastern Jin dynasty who loved horses for their spirit.

glosses.zh: 巡幸：皇帝出外巡视。
glosses.en: xún xìng: an emperor's journey to visit places.

glosses.zh: 新丰宫：指骊山脚下的华清宫，在新丰县一带。唐玄宗常去。
glosses.en: xīn fēng gōng: the Huaqing Palace below Mount Li, in Xinfeng county, which Xuanzong often visited.

glosses.zh: 翠华：用翠鸟羽毛装饰的旗子，是皇帝的仪仗。
glosses.en: cuì huá: banners decorated with kingfisher feathers, carried before the emperor.

glosses.zh: 拂天：飘到天上，形容旗子又高又多。
glosses.en: fú tiān: brushing the sky, showing how tall and many the banners were.

glosses.zh: 腾骧：马奔腾跳跃。
glosses.en: téng xiāng: galloping and leaping.

glosses.zh: 磊落：众多而雄壮的样子。
glosses.en: lěi luò: many and magnificent.

glosses.zh: 筋骨：马的体格和骨架。
glosses.en: jīn gǔ: a horse's build and frame.

glosses.zh: 献宝朝河宗：古书说周穆王向西巡游，到河宗那里献上宝玉。这里借指唐玄宗去世。
glosses.en: xiàn bǎo cháo hé zōng: an old story says King Mu of Zhou went west and offered jade to the river god. Here it stands for the death of Emperor Xuanzong.

glosses.zh: 射蛟：汉武帝曾在江中射死一条蛟龙。这里说皇帝再也不能出游打猎了。
glosses.en: shè jiāo: Emperor Wu of Han once shot a river dragon. Here it means the emperor will never ride out again.

glosses.zh: 金粟堆：金粟山，唐玄宗的陵墓泰陵就在这里。
glosses.en: jīn sù duī: Mount Jinsu, where Emperor Xuanzong's tomb lies.

glosses.zh: 龙媒：好马、骏马。汉武帝的《天马歌》说天马是龙的同类。
glosses.en: lóng méi: fine horses. A song of Emperor Wu of Han called heavenly horses kin of dragons.

glosses.zh: 鸟呼风：只剩下鸟在风中鸣叫，十分冷清。
glosses.en: niǎo hū fēng: only birds crying in the wind, lonely and still.

translation.zh: 从唐朝开国以来，画马的人里，
translation.en: Since the start of our dynasty, among all who painted horses,

translation.zh: 画得最神妙的，只能算江都王。
translation.en: the most wonderful was the Prince of Jiangdu alone.

translation.zh: 曹将军成名已经三十年了，
translation.en: General Cao has been famous for thirty years,

translation.zh: 人们又在他的画里看到了真正的神马。
translation.en: and in his work people see a true magic horse once more.

translation.zh: 他曾经给先帝的名马照夜白画像，
translation.en: He once painted the late emperor's horse, Night-Shining White,

translation.zh: 画成后龙池上一连十天雷声大作。
translation.en: and over Dragon Pond thunder rolled for ten days.

translation.zh: 宫中仓库里有一只深红色的玛瑙盘，
translation.en: From the palace storehouse came a deep red agate plate;

translation.zh: 婕妤传下皇帝的命令，才人把它取了出来。
translation.en: a palace lady passed on the order, and another fetched it.

translation.zh: 盘子赐给了将军，他拜谢之后回家，
translation.en: The plate was given to the general, who bowed his thanks and went home,

translation.zh: 从此请他作画的人送来的丝绸接连不断。
translation.en: and after that fine silks came flying after him one after another.

translation.zh: 皇亲贵族得到了他的画，
translation.en: When noble families got his paintings,

translation.zh: 才觉得自家的屏风有了光彩。
translation.en: they felt their screens begin to shine.

translation.zh: 从前有唐太宗的名马拳毛䯄，
translation.en: Long ago there was Emperor Taizong's horse Curly-Haired Gua,

translation.zh: 近来有郭家的名马狮子花。
translation.en: and lately the Guo family's horse Lion Flower.

translation.zh: 现在这幅新画里就画了这两匹马，
translation.en: Now this new painting shows these two,

translation.zh: 又让懂行的人看了久久赞叹。
translation.en: and again those who know gaze and sigh for a long time.

translation.zh: 这两匹都是能以一当万的战马，
translation.en: Both are war horses, each worth ten thousand,

translation.zh: 白绢上好像展开了一片无边的风沙。
translation.en: and across the white silk a wide land of wind and sand opens up.

translation.zh: 其余七匹马也都特别出众，
translation.en: The other seven horses are also superb,

translation.zh: 远看就像寒冷的天空里飘动着烟雾和雪花。
translation.en: like mist and snow moving across a cold sky.

translation.zh: 马蹄在长长的楸树道上踢踏奔跑，
translation.en: Their hooves stamp along a road lined with tall catalpa trees,

translation.zh: 管马的官员和仆人整齐地站成一排排。
translation.en: and grooms and stable hands stand in neat rows.

translation.zh: 多可爱啊，九匹马一匹比一匹神气，
translation.en: How lovely these nine horses are, each more spirited than the last,

translation.zh: 左右顾盼，神态高贵，气度沉稳。
translation.en: looking about, noble and proud, calm and steady.

translation.zh: 请问真心喜爱这幅画的人是谁？
translation.en: May I ask who loves this painting with all his heart?

translation.zh: 后来有韦讽，从前有支遁。
translation.en: Today there is Wei Feng, as long ago there was Zhi Dun.

translation.zh: 回想当年皇上巡游新丰宫的时候，
translation.en: I remember when the emperor travelled to the Xinfeng Palace,

translation.zh: 翠羽旗子高得拂着天，一路向东而来。
translation.en: his feathered banners brushing the sky as he came east.

translation.zh: 奔腾跳跃的骏马有三万匹，
translation.en: Thirty thousand horses galloped and leapt,

translation.zh: 个个都和这幅画里的马一样健壮。
translation.en: all as strong in bone as the horses in this picture.

translation.zh: 可是自从皇上像周穆王那样去拜见河神（去世）以后，
translation.en: But since the emperor went, like King Mu of old, to meet the river god,

translation.zh: 再也没有在江中射蛟龙的盛事了。
translation.en: there is no more shooting of dragons in the river.

translation.zh: 你没看见吗？金粟山前的松柏林里，
translation.en: Have you not seen, among the pines and cypresses before Mount Jinsu,

translation.zh: 骏马都已经走光了，只有鸟儿在风里鸣叫。
translation.en: the fine horses are all gone, and only birds cry in the wind?

background.zh: 这首诗一般认为写于唐代宗广德二年（764年），那时杜甫在成都。曹霸是唐玄宗时最有名的画马名家，做过将军。安史之乱以后，他失去官职，流落到四川，杜甫在成都和他相识。杜甫的朋友韦讽当时任录事，家里收藏着曹霸画的一幅九马图。杜甫在韦讽家看了这幅画，写下这首诗。同一时期他还写了《丹青引赠曹将军霸》。
background.en: This poem is usually dated to 764, when Du Fu was living in Chengdu. Cao Ba had been the most famous horse painter under Emperor Xuanzong, and had served as a general. After the An Lushan Rebellion he lost his post and drifted to Sichuan, where Du Fu met him. Du Fu's friend Wei Feng, who held the post of recorder, owned a painting by Cao Ba of nine horses. Du Fu saw it at Wei Feng's home and wrote this poem. Around the same time he also wrote another poem for Cao Ba, "Song of Painting, for General Cao Ba".

author_note.zh: 杜甫（712—770），唐代大诗人，被称为“诗圣”。他年轻时在长安见过唐朝最兴盛的样子，后来经历了安史之乱，四处漂泊。所以他写画、写马，也常常写到国家由盛转衰，心里满是怀念和伤感。
author_note.en: Du Fu (712–770) was a great Tang poet, often called the Sage of Poetry. As a young man in Chang'an he saw the Tang at its height. Then he lived through the An Lushan Rebellion and wandered from place to place. So even when he wrote about a painting or a horse, he often thought of how the country had fallen from glory, and his poems are full of longing and sadness.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗写的是一幅画，却像带着读者走进一个热闹又伤感的故事。开头先说画马的名家，再说曹霸有多受皇帝看重：画了照夜白，龙池都打起雷来；皇帝赏他玛瑙盘，贵族们抢着要他的画。然后才进入正题，一匹匹地看画里的九匹马：两匹战马气势逼人，白绢上好像刮起了风沙；另外七匹像寒空里的烟和雪；马夫们整齐地站着。九匹马个个神气，诗人看得入迷。最后笔锋一转，想起当年玄宗出游，三万匹骏马浩浩荡荡；如今皇帝已经去世，陵墓前只剩松柏和风中的鸟叫。从画中的好马，想到消失的盛世，热闹的开头和冷清的结尾一对比，让人格外感伤。
appreciation.en: This poem is about a painting, but it leads the reader into a story that is both lively and sad. It begins with the great horse painters, then tells how much the emperor valued Cao Ba. When he painted Night-Shining White, thunder rolled over Dragon Pond. The emperor gave him an agate plate, and noble families fought for his work. Only then does the poet look at the nine horses one by one. Two war horses look so fierce that wind and sand seem to blow across the white silk. The other seven are like mist and snow in a cold sky. The grooms stand in neat rows. Every horse is full of spirit, and the poet cannot look away. At the end the poem turns. He remembers the emperor's grand journeys, with thirty thousand fine horses. Now that emperor is dead. Before his tomb there are only pines and birds crying in the wind. From the fine horses in the picture, the poet thinks of a golden age that has vanished. The busy opening and the lonely ending make the sadness even deeper.
